https://mkraina.com/arinimal-an-enigma-by-m-k-raina/."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"Kamil writes that Mahmud Gaami is a historical fact and Arinimaal a conceived character."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"The article states that all this is to show that the poem 'åríní rang gom shràvan híyè' is that of Mehmud Gaami and not that of Arinimaal."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"There are numerous instances to show that verses of various poets have been recorded differently at different places."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"Amin Kamil accepts this in Chapter 4 of his book 'Kulyat Habba Khatoon'."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"On the controversy regarding this poem, Azad says that we often find such lamentation in the verses of Arinimaal."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"Azad says that this poem has been published in the name of Mehmud Gaami, but the circumstantial evidence and peculiarity of the ode tell us that it reflects the emotions of Mrs. Bhawani Das."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"T.N.Kaul in his book 'Gems of Kashmiri Literature' writes that it will not be out of place to mention here that some cussed and overzealous literary critics have wrongly attributed one of Arinimaal's most pathetic ditties – 'åríní rang gom shràvan híyè', to her contemporary, Mahmud Gami (1765-1855)."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"T.N.Kaul further writes that a 90 year old descendant of the Kachru family told Kaul in an exclusive interview in Srinagar in 1987 that Arinimaal had herself also recorded a large number of her poems while she remained separated from her beloved at Palhalan village."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"T.N.Kaul further writes that after Arinimaal's death, these creations were handed over to the old man's ancestors who kept them in safe custody."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"T.N.Kaul further writes that in view of the atrocities perpetrated by the Afghans in the closing years of their rule on the civilian population and the consequent risk of damage to the invaluable poems, the Kachrus were obliged to deposit this treasure in a 'Chah' (dry well) near the Hari Parbat hill."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"Shashi Shekhar Toshakhani, in his book 'Kashmiri Sahitya ka Itihas', writes that this is one of the most popular Kashmiri songs, because of its melody and compassion."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"Toshakhani writes that it is so popular that Mehmud Gaami, a famous poet, has also used its few lines in one of his poems."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"Toshakhani writes that because of this, some critics like Ghulam Nabi Khayal consider it to be originally of Mehmud Gaami."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"Toshakhani writes that by detailed analysis and comparison, Autar Krishen Rehbar has proved that the basic lines are that of Arinimaal only."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"Toshakhani writes that Rehbar has clearly shown that these are two different poems, only its refrain, 'åríní rang gom shràvan híyè', is common in both."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"There are several instances where verse of one poet has wrongly (may be inadvertently) been attributed to other."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"Commenting on the confusion regarding year of birth of Mehmud Gaami, Naji Munawar writes that after going through the manuscripts titled 'Yakh Hakayath' and 'Ponpuri' we can come to the conclusion that either the Mehmud's era has wrongly been calculated ….. or, there has been another poet named Mehmud, whose verse has got messed up with that of Mehmud Gaami, like, some of Maqbool Amritsari's poetry was being printed in the name of Maqbool Kralawari."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"Regarding 'kävi víhínúm aríníní …' poem, Kamil says that this is said to have been attributed to Arinimaal only because it contained the word 'Arini'."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"Kamil says that it is clear that this poem was not attached to her as late as 1946."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"Azad, on the other hand, assumes the poem to be that of Munshi Bhawani Das."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"In another twist to the issue, Kamil feels pleasure in putting this poem in the basket of Habba Khatoon."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"Kamil says that this poem is also said to be that of Habba Khatoon, and genuinely so, because she has, during her royal times, composed some poems with twisted words (lafzû gyúnd kåríth)."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"Kamil says that this poem also contains the same twist."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"Kamil does not mention who told him so and with what proof."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"Another point of contention has been the verse 'tarvûní margû tû vasvûní bàlò', in the poem 'mê shòkû yàrû sûndí bårímas pyàlay', as it appeared in the Pratap Magazine edited by Jia Lal Kaul in the year 1936."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"Amin Kamil, as also Akhtar Mohi-ud-Din, are of the view that the verse should read 'khasvûní margû tu vasvûní bàlò'."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"They use it as a proof of bungling by Mr. Kaul."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"The article states that a 'marg' is the plain area at the top of a mountain or between the mountains, which can only be crossed and not ascended."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"Hence, 'tarvûní margû' is more authentic."},{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"The supplied evidence record has doc_ref D9."}]},"candidate":{"evidence_refs":["W12"],"statement":"Amin Kamil wrote that Mahmud Gaami is a historical fact and Arinimaal a conceived character."}}
